1.
List revised.

2. Heard Sri Rajiv Kumar Tripathi, learned counsel for the revisionist and Sri Shashikant Pandey,
learned counsel for the State and perused the material on record.

3. The present revision under Sections 397/401 Cr.P.C. has been preferred by the revisionist- Shiv Vishal @ Falva @ Falka against the judgement and order dated 25.07.2008 passed by Additional District & Sessions Judge (Court No.1), Hamirpur in Criminal Appeal No. 22 of 2007 (Shiv Vishal @
Falva @ Falka vs. State) by which the said appeal has been partly allowed which was preferred against the judgement and order dated 16.08.2007 passed by the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Hamirpur in Criminal Case No. 1274 of 2006 (State of U.P. vs. Shiv Vishal @ Falva @
Shiv Vishal @ Falva @ Falka vs State Of U.P. on 28 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96983699/
1 Falka), Police Station Khanna, District Hamirpur whereby the revisionist-accused was convicted and sentenced under Section 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act for six months rigorous imprisonment & fine of Rs. 1000/- and in default of payment of fine to further undergo 15 days additional imprisonment.

sentences.text: 4. The facts of the case are that the Food Inspector Sri N.D. Khare visited the shop of the revisionist on 12.11.1987 at about 2 p.m. and found him displaying and selling mustard oil.
On a suspicion of the same to be adulterated he purchased the same on which the accused denied his signature.
He took a receipt of the same.
He preserved the material in three bottles in equal quantity and completed the proceedings and sent one of the same to the food analyst for its testing.

The food analyst vide his note dated 05.01.1988 opined that the sample was found having excess amount of butryro refractometer contents, saponification and iodine and the sample contained around 60% of Tisi oil.
The sample was thus considered to be adulterated.

Sanction was taken from the C.M.O.
concerned and a complaint dated 14.09.1989 was filed by the food analyst before the court concerned.

5. The trial court framed charges against the revisionist vide order dated 08.02.1996 for offences under Section 16 (i) (a) (i) (ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 to which the accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
6. The trial started in which the complainant N.D. Khare was examined as P.W.1 and Ramdarash Yadav the Senior Clerk was examined as P.W.-2.
7. The accused in his statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C. stated of being falsely implicated in the present case and stated of a case being initiated due to ill-will.
He produced Siddh Gopal as D.W.-1 before the trial court who stated that on 12.11.1987 no Food Inspector came to the shop and no Inspector purchased any oil from the shop.

8. The trial court finding the prosecution to be beyond reasonable doubt convicted the revisionist under Section 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act for six months rigorous imprisonment & fine of Rs. 1000/- and in default of payment of fine to further undergo 15 days additional imprisonment

9. An appeal being Criminal Appeal No. 22 of 2007 (Shiv Vishal @ Falva @ Falka vs. State) was preferred against the judgement and order of conviction dated 16.08.2007 passed by the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Hamirpur in Criminal Case No. 1274 of 2006 (State of U.P. vs. Shiv Vishal @ Falva @ Falka) which stood dismissed.

sentences.text: The present revision has thus been filed against the said judgement and orders.

10. Learned counsel for the revisionist submitted that the trial court was in error in convicting and sentencing the revisionist and even the trial court was in error in dismissing the appeal of the revisionist in as much as the sample of the alleged mustard oil was taken on 12.11.1987 after which the report of the Public Analyst is dated 05.01.1988 and then a complaint was filed on 14.09.1989 after which notice under Section 13 (2) of the Food Adulteration Act is alleged to have been sent to Shiv Vishal @ Falva @ Falka vs State Of U.P. on 28 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96983699/
2 the revisionist on 16.06.1990.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is submitted that as such the sending of notice under Section 13 (2)
of the Food Adulteration Act is after about 2 years & 5 months of the report of the Public Analyst.
It is submitted that even otherwise there is nothing on record to show that the said notice has been served upon the revisionist.

It is submitted that since the notice under Section 13 (2) of the Food Adulteration Act has been sent after an unexplained delay of about 2 years & 5 months from the date of the report of the Public Analyst coupled with the fact that there is nothing on record to show that the same has reached the revisionist, the valuable right of the revisionist for exercising his rights under Section 13 (2) of the Food Adulteration Act gets forfeited.
It is submitted that delay of about 2 years & 5 months as alleged by P.W.-2 in sending of the notice under Section 13 (2) of the Food Adulteration Act to the revisionist is unexplained.

It is submitted that since the revisionist could not get a right to get another sample of the item tested by the Central Food Laboratory, his valuable right under Section 13 (2) of the Food Adulteration Act is forfeited.
It is submitted that there is no finding of the trial court concerned that the said notice as allegedly send to the revisionist has been delivered to the revisionist.

It is submitted that as such looking to the fact that the notice under Section 13 (2) of the Food Adulteration Act as alleged to have been sent after a delay of about 2 years & 5 months, the sample of mustard oil naturally decays.
It is submitted that the revisionist is thus entitled to the benefit of doubt.
11. Learned counsel for the State has been heard and trial court records tagged with the present revision have been perused.

12. After having heard learned counsel for the parties and perusing the record, it is evident that notice under Section 13 (2) of the Food Adulteration Act is said to have sent on 16.06.1990 after a complaint was filed on 14.09.1989 for a report of a Public Analyst dated 05.01.1988.
The notice has been sent belatedly without any plausible explanation.
The food item as collected is mustard oil which in normal course decays with passage of time.
13. In view of the same, the revisionist deserves to be extended the benefit of doubt.
14. The present revision is allowed.

The impugned judgement and order dated 25.07.2008 passed by Additional District & Sessions Judge (Court No.1), Hamirpur and the impugned judgement and order dated 16.08.2007 passed by the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Hamirpur in Criminal Case No. 1274 of 2006 are hereby set aside.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 15. The revisionist- Shiv Vishal @ Falva @ Falka is acquitted of the charge levelled against him.
The revisionist is on bail.
His bail bond is cancelled and sureties discharged.
16. Office is directed to transmit the copy of this judgement along with the trial court records to the concerned trial court forthwith for its compliance and necessary action.
17. The file be consigned to records.
